learning: Iteration 9 (0.035 m, kp 0.7) scored 64.78, so the wheel-radius trend is downward above 0.030 m. If 0.025 m beats 73.33, the optimum is below 0.030 m and the next test is 0.022 m. If it falls back, 0.030 m is the local optimum and sensor size (16 mm) is the next single-variable test.
notes: Single-variable wheel_radius test at 0.025 m on the iteration 7 design, with kp scaled up to 0.96 to offset the lower turn gain. Controller is otherwise unchanged so the score is comparable with 73.33.
rationale: Iteration 9 tested wheel_radius 0.035 m with kp 0.7 and scored 64.78, below the 73.33 best at 0.030 m. Oval progress rose (0.227 to 0.273) while s-bend (0.194 to 0.078) and slalom fell, so larger wheels help straight-line speed and hurt bend response. The Builder's intent is to test the other side at 0.025 m. Turn rate per unit PWM difference scales with wheel radius, so 0.025/0.030 = 0.833 lowers effective steering gain by about 17 percent. I raise kp from 0.8 to 0.96 to hold the iteration 7 bend response, the reverse of the iteration 9 adjustment. kd stays 0.15 and ki 0 because no steady offset has been observed. base_speed 1.5, last_direction and the sensor weights are unchanged. Expected, not measured: s-bend and slalom progress recover, oval progress falls slightly, and max_error moves toward 0.060 m. The main risk is that the smaller wheels cut ground speed enough that the course cannot be covered in time at base_speed 1.5.
